{
  "subtype": "exploratory_data_analysis",
  "focus_variable": "resolution_efficiency",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "incident_category",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Well-separated interpretable categories, but the query already names 'category' as a grouping axis and the original table has a 'category' column. This largely restates an existing focus/grouping dimension rather than opening a new relationship."
    },
    {
      "name": "affected_asset_type",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "External associational variable with clean, well-separated categories (printer, monitor, server, laptop...). One can segment resolution efficiency by asset type and compare meaningfully. Adds a genuinely new dimension beyond the query's stated axes."
    },
    {
      "name": "failure_symptom_type",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable, well-separated symptom categories that plausibly relate to how quickly incidents resolve. Grouping efficiency by symptom is an informative exploratory comparison, though 'malfunction_general' dominates (310/500), weakening some contrasts."
    },
    {
      "name": "self_resolved_by_assignee",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Clean binary split, but 'self resolved by assignee' is essentially a facet of the resolution process itself, closely tied to the efficiency focus rather than an external associational variable to compare against it."
    },
    {
      "name": "software_trigger_present",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable binary segmentation that is external to the focus; efficiency can be compared for software-triggered vs not. Reasonable exploratory contrast, though the 54/446 imbalance limits the strength of comparison."
    },
    {
      "name": "requires_replacement",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": false,
      "rationale": "Conceptually relevant (replacement likely lengthens resolution), but the near-constant distribution (14 true / 486 false) means the 'true' segment is too small for a meaningful, well-supported comparison."
    }
  ],
  "n_predictors": 4,
  "relationship_informativeness": 0.55,
  "rationale": "The set contains interpretable, well-separated categorical variables and several offer genuine external axes (affected_asset_type, failure_symptom_type, software_trigger_present) along which resolution efficiency can be segmented and compared. However, quality is diluted: incident_category largely restates an existing grouping axis, self_resolved_by_assignee is a facet of the resolution process rather than an independent associational variable, and requires_replacement is too near-constant (14/500) to support meaningful comparison. Several binaries are also heavily imbalanced, limiting contrast strength. Moderately informative for exploratory relationship discovery, but not strongly so."
}
